Rufus Bature, has warned that any member of the party found in anti-party activities would be sanctioned to serve as a deterrent to others.
Bature made the disclosure in Jos during a courtesy visit by the director-general of the Tinubu/Shettima, Mutfwang/Piyo Campaign Organisation, Sir Joseph Ari, and members of the campaign council to the party secretariat.
He said the party was aware of certain individuals involved in anti-party activities, adding that the party is governed by laws and the law would take its course.
“The party is aware of certain individuals that are engaging anti-party activities. We are governed by laws. At the appropriate time, sanctions will be meted out on those the party finds wanting in one way or the other.
“We will be governed by laws and we must respect the laws that have created us as a body. Nobody is bigger than the party. All of us are under the party and we are subject to the rules and obligations of the party,” Bature said.
Earlier, Ari said the courtesy visit was to inform the party leadership of the inauguration of the campaign council and to seek the blessings of the party.
He said it was a pleasure to be at the party secretariat to visit the leaders of the party in the state, and thanked the chairman for hastening the process of the meeting despite the very short notice.
Ari informed the chairman that the Tinubu/Shettima, Mutfwang/Piyo Campaign Council has been inaugurated by the governor of Plateau State, Barr Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang.
He disclosed that the campaign council has since swung into action, met with all the directors, drawn up an action plan and presented it to their principals who have given their note and approval for the execution and prosecution of the campaigns.
Ari announced that the execution of the action plan would begin with seeking the face of God.
He said on Friday that the council would present the action plan and seek the face of God at the mosque during the Juma’at prayers, while there will be a thanksgiving service on Sunday.
He said the council intends to take its campaigns to the nooks and crannies of the state and requested the party chairman to arrange a meeting with the candidates of the APC.
Ari stressed that this is one of the first times Plateau is taking its place in the mainstream of national politics, and there is need for the people to stand behind the leaders by ensuring massive votes so that Plateau will have a great sitting arrangement at the negotiation table.
He noted that the leader of the party in the state, Gov. Caleb Mutfwang, and the national chairman of the party, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, have since closed ranks and are working together.
As a founding member of the APC in Plateau State, Ari called on the chairman and members of the Working Committee to ensure enforcement of the provisions for sanctions against erring members, particularly those engaged in anti-party activities.
